metadata.description: Answer as a page in its own browser tab (page_url), not as a chat table

context.domain_knowledge:
# Page in its own tab (page_tab)
The answer the user asked for is **a page**, not a message in this chat. A page lives in its own browser tab. The chat shows **only** the page card (the same way a map shows only the map card). Do not write the answer in the bubble: no report, no table, no pasted HTML. The click opens the page.
## How Do the data work as usual. Then, in the **same** `relaxaicode` that returns the rows, put the url of the page on that result. Pass those rows into `page_url`. A call with no rows does not lay the page out (the server waits and uses the rows when they exist). Do not call `page_url` on an empty `data` and then ship a second table without the url::
rows = [...] # the rows of this answer result = { 'data': rows, 'summary': '…', 'page_url': page_url(rows, 'what they asked for the page'), }
- `page_url(rows, instruction)` returns a url, the same way `map_pins_url` does. `rows` are the rows of this answer. Design returns a template; the server fills `const DATA` from those rows. - A brand new page passes `new=True`. - The server paints the link from `page_url`. Nothing else is needed.
## Changing the page already open "Add this", "remove that", "make it dark", "group the cards by brand": a change to the open page uses `page_edit`. It reuses the same tab and Design writes only the changes, so it takes seconds instead of minutes::
result = { 'summary': '…', 'page_url': page_edit('what to change on the page'), }
- When the figures are already on the page (layout, colours, order, a column or section to hide, a chart of what is shown), call it **without rows** and do **not** query the data again. - When the change needs figures the page does not have, query them and pass them: `page_edit('add the mileage per driver', rows)`. - A different subject or "a new page" is not a change: that is `page_url` with `new=True`. - `page_edit` returns an empty string when no page is open. Then lay the page out with `page_url(rows, …, new=True)`.
## Hard rules - Do **not** write the page yourself: no hand-written HTML, no style block, no `__untrusted_html_preview__`. The template is returned by the design provider inside `page_url`, not by you. - Do **not** deliver the same answer as only a chat table. If a page was asked for, the result carries `page_url`. - Figures come from `rows`. Pass them into `page_url`. Design returns a reusable template (`const DATA`, and `const TITLE` when it writes one). The server always writes this run's rows into that slot — the first turn and a later slash do the same. Design may use a short sample or fictional rows with the same keys. The server only writes `#pns-page-rows` if the template has no slot. Never invent a number. - A plain data question stays in the chat and does **not** call `page_url`. Intent is semantic, not a fixed phrase list.
## When there is no page (soft fail) `page_url` returns an **empty string** when the page could not be laid out. That is not an error and it does not stop this answer::
href = page_url(rows, 'what they asked for the page') result = {'data': rows, 'summary': '…'} if href: result['page_url'] = href
If the url is empty, keep the rows. Do **not** invent a reason — not Design, not a missing provider, not a missing tick. The server already wrote the cause in Historial IA. Do not retry `page_url`, do not lay the page out yourself, and do not ask another provider for it.
If `page_url` is not among the sandbox helpers at all, the canvas is not installed: answer in the chat and say so.
